h1: Independent Bo's — Bohemian Bungalows on the Rocks at the Cheapest End of White Sand Beach
intro: At the very north end of White Sand Beach, where the sand gives way to big rocks and forest climbing the hillside, sits Independent Bo's — a backpacker guesthouse famous for its full-on bohemian style: murals of dragons, monkeys and abstract faces across the walls, and over 20 rooms staggered up the rocks and slope, no two alike. The draw is a seafront position many call one of the prettiest spots on the island, plus a cafe-bar where you can watch the sunset over the water. It's the cheapest place to stay on White Sand Beach, from about ฿400–500/night for a fan room. But know going in: this is a raw, basic place with a 3-night minimum stay and no children.

body.html: Independent Bo's isn't a resort and never tries to be. It's a backpacker guesthouse at the far north end of White Sand Beach, right where the sand turns into big boulders and green forest climbs the steep slope. Over 20 rooms are built into the hillside and perched on the sea rocks, and no two look the same. The walls are covered in painted dragons, monkeys and abstract faces, with flags, fishing nets, pinwheels, driftwood and assorted curios everywhere — heaven if you love raw, handmade character, a bit too cluttered if you want clean lines and order.

The location is what reviewers talk about most. From the bar and terraces you look straight out over the sea and rocks to clear water, and there's a sunset spot many rate as one of the finest on Koh Chang. One traveler who'd stayed in hotels all over the world wrote they had nothing bad to say about the view and atmosphere. The flip side of sitting on the rocks at the end of the beach: reaching the main strip of restaurants and bars in the middle of White Sand Beach means a roughly 7-minute walk along the sand, which is trickier at high tide and after dark.

"Sipping a beer at the bar on the rocks as the sun softened, looking out at clear water and distant islands, chatting with travelers from the other side of the world — you don't get that from an air-conditioned resort."

Rooms are all fan-cooled with mosquito nets and double mattresses. The most basic rooms share cold-water bathrooms, while the deluxe rooms up on stilts have en-suite hot showers and private balconies. Prices start around ฿400–500/night for a basic fan room and climb with the room type and season. This really is the cheapest stay on White Sand Beach, and the charm is in how different every room is — some get full sea views, others tuck into the forest, so which room you choose makes a big difference to the experience.

The heart of the place is the beachfront cafe and bar, which buzzes in the evenings. It's a natural gathering point, so it's easy to make new friends and pick up Koh Chang tips from the locals and the friendly owner. That social vibe is the main reason backpackers pick it. Food and drinks are cheap, and many nights run long with music and conversation — better suited to solo travelers and couples who want to meet people than to anyone after quiet privacy.

Honestly, from real guest reviews: this is a raw place that won't suit everyone. Facilities are very basic, some rooms involve a steep climb, and because it sits in forest on the hill, ants, mosquitoes, other bugs and humidity come with the territory. Some reviews complain about cleanliness and rooms looking run-down with age. Two recurring points: the 3-night minimum stay, which resets if you change rooms, and the owner's manner — some find her warm and helpful, others have caught her on an off day and found her abrupt. Expect that experience to swing.

Overall, Independent Bo's suits backpackers and rough-and-ready travelers who value the seafront location, artist atmosphere and low price over comfort and polish. If you're on Koh Chang to spend your days outside — swimming, beach-walking, meeting people — and only need somewhere to close your eyes at night, this gives you a position and character you can't buy from an air-conditioned room at the same price. But if you need air-con, a spotless bathroom, or you're traveling with young kids, this isn't it — pick a different tier of stay instead.

A tip from the reviews: the place runs mostly on walk-ins and choosing your room on the spot, so if you can, look at a few rooms before deciding — they vary a lot in view, stair-steepness and whether the bathroom is en-suite or shared. Go in expecting the 3-night minimum, and bring mosquito repellent and a small torch, because the hillside paths get quite dark at night.

Its charm is the view, the rocks, the no-two-alike rooms and the buzzing bar. But accept that facilities are very basic, there are bugs and humidity, a 3-night minimum stay, and no children.

faqTitle: Independent Bo's Koh Chang — Frequently Asked Questions

faq.q: Where exactly is Independent Bo's on Koh Chang?
faq.a: It's at the far north end of White Sand Beach (Haad Sai Khao), where the sand turns into rocks and forest climbs the hill. It's about a 7-minute walk along the sand to the restaurants and bars in the middle of the beach, and roughly 20 minutes by car from Ao Sapparot Pier (the island ferry point). The beach walk is harder at high tide and after dark.

faq.q: How much does Independent Bo's cost and what rooms are there?
faq.a: From about ฿400–500/night for a fan room — the cheapest stay on White Sand Beach. Basic rooms share a cold-water bathroom; deluxe rooms on stilts have en-suite hot showers and balconies. There are over 20 individually designed rooms, with prices moving by room type and season — best to view a room in person before choosing.

faq.q: Is there a minimum stay, and does it accept children?
faq.a: Yes — there's a 3-night minimum stay, and it resets if you change rooms. The property has a no-children policy, leaning into an adult backpacker atmosphere centered on the bar. If you're on a short 1–2 night trip or traveling as a family, it likely won't suit you — look at other stays on the island.

faq.q: Who is Independent Bo's right and wrong for?
faq.a: Right for backpackers and rough-and-ready travelers who value seafront location, artist atmosphere, a low price and meeting people. Wrong for anyone who needs air-con, a spotless bathroom, quiet privacy, or who's traveling with young kids — facilities are very basic, with bugs and humidity that come with a forested hillside setting.

faq.q: What are cleanliness and bugs like?
faq.a: Because it sits in hillside forest, ants, mosquitoes, bugs and humidity are normal, and some reviews note rooms looking dated. Ask to see the actual room before you walk in, pick the one in the best condition, and bring mosquito repellent and a small torch, since the hillside paths are dark at night.

faq.q: Can you book ahead, or is it walk-in only?
faq.a: It runs mostly on walk-ins, choosing your room on the spot. In high season (November–April) it gets busy and the good rooms fill fast, so arrive early. In the rainy season (May–October) it's quieter and easier to negotiate, though some days bring heavy rain and the hillside paths get slippery.
